sections.title: ADMISSION SUMMARY
sections.content:
Dear Doctor, Thank you for your ongoing care of patient, a <CIT id="c1">58-year-old female</CIT> who presented to the Emergency Department at our hospital on today's date with a <CIT id="c2">2-month history of knee pain</CIT>.

Her primary complaint was <CIT id="c3">acute onset knee pain during a yoga session</CIT> where her knee and hip were flexed. She described the pain as feeling <CIT id="c4">"broken", 10/10 in severity, non-migratory, and making it difficult to walk</CIT>. Initial investigations included a <CIT id="c5">knee X-ray which showed no findings</CIT>, and she was provided with <CIT id="c6">crutches</CIT>.

Currently, her pain is <CIT id="c7">low, though still present with walking</CIT>. She has been managing her pain with <CIT id="c8">ibuprofen</CIT>. Her past medical history is notable for <CIT id="c9">chronic wrist pain treated with two steroid injections</CIT>. She is <CIT id="c10">perimenopausal and takes estrogen replacement, along with turmeric, glucosamine, and evening primrose oil supplements</CIT>. Given her improved pain and stable condition, she is suitable for discharge.

sections.title: DISCHARGE PLAN
sections.content:
DISCHARGE PLAN

1. Discharge Destination: Patient is discharged home.

2. New Medications: No new medications prescribed. Please continue current medications as appropriate.

3. Follow-up Arrangements:
   - Please arrange for a review with her General Practitioner within 1-2 weeks for ongoing management of her knee pain.

4. Safety Netting:
   - Please seek medical attention if she experiences worsening knee pain, new swelling, redness, warmth, inability to bear weight, or any signs of infection.

Kind Regards,
Dr [Name]
Emergency Medicine JMO
